findings.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:168 — [P1 C100] `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config,` discards the normalized `config` assembled at lines 160–162, so whenever `schedule_type` is present every produced occurrence publishes the raw stored sentinel instead of the display value and the event schema drifts from its intended representation.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:93 — [P3 C100] `checkins = MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[c["id"] for c in previous_checkins])` makes every threshold-triggered occurrence path load the same check-ins a second time after lines 37–48 already queried them, doubling database round trips and row materialization on a volume-sensitive path; the strongest rebuttal is that `.values(...)` keeps the first read light, but it loses because full model instances are immediately required, so the dict/cast bridge at lines 37–48 and this requery can be deleted in favor of one sliced model query reused for threshold checks and occurrence creation.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:168 — [P1 C100] The serializer computes a normalized copy with verbatim `config["schedule_type"] = monitor_environment.monitor.get_schedule_type_display()` but returns verbatim `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config,`, so every occurrence whose monitor config contains `schedule_type` emits the raw stored value instead of the display value and the intended normalization is absent from the event context.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:93 — [P3 C100] Advisory: `checkins = MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[c["id"] for c in previous_checkins])` adds a redundant database read on every threshold-one and already-ERROR failure even though `failed_checkin` is already the sole model needed; the strongest rebuttal is that one query path keeps iteration uniform, but it loses because `checkins = [failed_checkin]` produces the identical one-item loop in those branches, and the deletion test of substituting that existing instance leaves every occurrence argument unchanged while removing one query per failure.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py:8 — [P2 C75] `from sentry.monitors.logic.incidents import try_incident_threshold` replaces the established `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and `SimpleCheckIn` bindings without compatibility aliases, so any existing direct import or monkeypatch of those names from `mark_failed` now fails with `ImportError` or `AttributeError` even though the stated objective is only to reorganize the logic; the strongest rebuttal is that this repository has no remaining callers, but that loses because a behavior-preserving refactor cannot assume externally imported Python module symbols are unused without explicit acceptance of the interface break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:168 — [P1 C100] The serializer computes a normalized copy with verbatim `config["schedule_type"] = monitor_environment.monitor.get_schedule_type_display()` but returns verbatim `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config,`, so every occurrence whose monitor config contains `schedule_type` emits the raw stored value instead of the display value and the intended normalization is absent from the event context.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at lines 163-171 in incident_occurrence.py, the function creates a copy of config with `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()`, then conditionally modifies `config['schedule_type']` to the display value, but then returns a dict that uses `'config': monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original, not the modified copy). This means the schedule_type normalization is never actually included in the returned context - it's a clear bug where the wrong variable is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:93 — [P3 C100] Advisory: `checkins = MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[c["id"] for c in previous_checkins])` adds a redundant database read on every threshold-one and already-ERROR failure even though `failed_checkin` is already the sole model needed; the strongest rebuttal is that one query path keeps iteration uniform, but it loses because `checkins = [failed_checkin]` produces the identical one-item loop in those branches, and the deletion test of substituting that existing instance leaves every occurrence argument unchanged while removing one query per failure.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in the `try_incident_threshold` function in incidents.py, when `failure_issue_threshold == 1` or when `monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR`, the code creates a `previous_checkins` list containing only the `failed_checkin` data, then queries the database again with `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[c['id'] for c in previous_checkins])` to get the same check-in object that's already available as `failed_checkin`. This is a valid performance concern - the database query is redundant in these specific code paths since `failed_checkin` is already a MonitorCheckIn model instance. However, this is a refactoring/optimization suggestion rather than a bug - the code functions correctly, just with an unnecessary database query in certain paths.
